target_audience: Executive Stakeholders and Science Policy Advisors

slides.title: Solar System: Planetary Exploration
planned_key_points: Solar System Overview
Planetary Exploration History
Future Missions

slides.title: How the Solar System Works
slides.visual_prompt: A high-resolution, cinematic 3D illustration of the solar system showing the Sun at the center with planets in their orbits, glowing orbital paths, and a deep space background with subtle nebula clouds.
planned_key_points: Gravitational Dynamics: How the Sun anchors the system
Orbital Mechanics: The dance of planets and moons
Energy Distribution: Solar radiation and planetary heat

slides.title: Planetary Orbits & Dynamics
slides.visual_prompt: A detailed scientific diagram showing elliptical planetary orbits around the Sun, with vector arrows indicating velocity and gravitational pull, clean white lines on a dark blue background.
planned_key_points: Kepler's Laws: Understanding elliptical paths
Orbital Resonance: Gravitational interactions between bodies
Velocity & Distance: The relationship between speed and orbit duration

slides.title: Comparative Planetary Analysis
slides.visual_prompt: A clean, professional infographic comparing the characteristics of inner terrestrial planets versus outer gas giants, using icons for temperature, size, and atmosphere.
planned_key_points: Inner vs Outer Planets Comparison
Atmospheric Composition Table
Gravity and Surface Conditions

slides.title: Solar System Formation
slides.visual_prompt: A dramatic artistic representation of the early solar system, showing a swirling protoplanetary disk around a young, bright Sun, with glowing dust and gas clouds.
planned_key_points: Nebular Hypothesis: The birth of the solar system from a molecular cloud
Accretion Process: How dust and gas formed protoplanets
Early Solar System: The chaotic environment of the young Sun

slides.title: Planetary Evolution
slides.visual_prompt: A split-screen illustration showing the evolution of a planet from a molten, volcanic state to a cooled, geologically active world with an atmosphere.
planned_key_points: Planetary Differentiation: How cores, mantles, and crusts formed
Geological Activity: Volcanism and tectonic shifts over eons
Atmospheric Evolution: The transition from primordial to secondary atmospheres

slides.title: Earth & Jupiter: Exploration Capabilities
planned_key_points: Earth's Habitable Zone: Conditions for life
Jupiter's Gravitational Influence: Protecting the inner system
Exploration Challenges: Distance and radiation shielding

slides.title: Executive Summary & Future Directions
planned_key_points: Summary of Key Findings
Upcoming Exploration Missions (Europa Clipper, Mars Sample Return)
The Future of Interplanetary Travel
